newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Monday were slow, with light bids at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00 to $69.00, feedlot sources said.
"There's a few buyers out there looking around, but they're not showing a lot of interest," a Kansas cattle feeder said.

Fed cattle in the Texas Panhandle, particularly around the Hereford and Amarillo area, were struggling with muddy pens following heavy rain and snow late last week. The conditions limited weight gains, several sources said.
There was talk that some owners were taking cattle off showlists to give them a chance to recover from the unusual spring snowstorm, Panhandle sources said.
"It's just sloppy out there and cattle are weighing up light," one source said.
Muddy conditions were not expected to last long amid forecasts for temperatures in the 70s Monday, cattle feeders said, but it could take a week for some cattle to recover.
Fed cattle prices this week could be underpinned by reduced market-ready supplies. But that support could be offset by packers' adequate live supplies.
Active sales last week ahead of the late-week storm an brisk sales the previous week contributed to relatively ample packer-held cattle inventories, sources said.
